title: The nonvanishing locus of an element of an invertible module over an affine scheme is affine
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and N an invertible R-module, meaning an R-module that is finite projective of rank 1 (equivalently, locally free of rank 1 on a cover of Spec(R) by standard opens D(f)). Let Sym_R(N) have canonical map iota as in [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property]. For s in N, let A=Sym_R(N) and B=A/(iota(s)-1)A. Then the morphism Spec(B) to Spec(R) [def-weil-affine-spectrum] identifies Spec(B) with the open subset V={p in Spec(R) | s is not in pN}; equivalently, V is affine.

proof.text: Choose a finite standard-open cover $D(f_i)$ of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ on which $N_{f_i}$ is free of rank one, and choose a basis $e_i$ there. Write the image of $s$ as $a_i e_i$ for $a_i\in R_{f_i}$. At a prime of $D(f_i)$, $s\notin\mathfrak pN$ exactly when $a_i\notin\mathfrak pR_{f_i}$, so $V\cap D(f_i)=D(a_i)$ inside $\operatorname{Spec}R_{f_i}$.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PV, proof: invertible module and the open V

proof.text: Localize the defining quotient $B=\operatorname{Sym}_R(N)/(\iota(s)-1)$ at $f_i$. Localization of a quotient and symmetric-algebra base change give $B_{f_i}\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{R_{f_i}}(N_{f_i})/(\iota(s_{f_i})-1)$. Since $N_{f_i}=R_{f_i}e_i$, the free-module symmetric-algebra identification makes this $R_{f_i}[t]/(a_it-1)$, with $t$ corresponding to $e_i$.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PV, proof: the construction of B commutes with base change

proof.text: By the affine fibre product identification, the base change of $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ along $\operatorname{Spec}R_{f_i}\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_RR_{f_i})=\operatorname{Spec}(B_{f_i})\to\operatorname{Spec}R_{f_i}$. The polynomial-quotient localization theorem identifies $R_{f_i}[t]/(a_it-1)$ with $(R_{f_i})_{a_i}$, compatibly with the map from $R_{f_i}$. Thus this base change is the principal-localization open immersion with image $D(a_i)=V\cap D(f_i)$.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PV, proof: the local identification of Spec B with V

proof.text: The finite standard-open cover $\{D(f_i)\}$ is fpqc: its maps are flat localizations, and every affine open has a finite affine refinement by intersections with the $D(f_i)$. The fpqc descent criterion for open immersions therefore makes $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ an open immersion. Its image meets every $D(f_i)$ in $D(a_i)$ by the preceding steps, hence its image is exactly $V$. By the definition of an open immersion it identifies $\operatorname{Spec}B$ with the open subscheme $V$, so $V$ is affine.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PV, proof: final identification of Spec B with V
